title: Tracking Misinformation: Ukraine Map and Peace Terms
summary: We are aware of posts circulating on social media that attribute publication of this map to The New York Times, alongside claims that The Times published a report outlining Russian peace terms…
body_markdown:
The New York Times did not publish this map of Ukraine or a report about a set of proposed Russian peace terms circulating on social media this week.


We are aware of posts circulating on social media that attribute publication of this map to The New York Times, alongside claims that The Times published a report outlining Russian peace terms, including recognition of occupied Ukrainian territories and a reduction of Ukraine’s military, to U.S. President Donald Trump.


The New York Times has not published an article outlining this specific set of Russian peace terms, nor have we published this map. Our[latest report](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/17/us/trump-putin-russia-sanctions.html?searchResultPosition=12) on Russia’s negotiations with the U.S. noted that when President Trump’s envoys sat down with Vladimir V. Putin at the Kremlin this month, Mr. Putin claimed Russian troops would capture Ukraine’s entire Donbas region within months. He also said Russia was poised to pummel Ukraine’s electricity grid. Readers can follow our latest reporting on the Russia-Ukraine war[here](https://www.nytimes.com/news-event/ukraine-russia) .
